the PSA is a major immunogen of L. infantum and that the leucine-rich repeats are the main antigenic region of the PSA.
the leucine rich region of the PSA protein is the main immunogenic region in dogs and humans with visceral leishamaniasis caused by Leishmania infantu.
the immunodominants of the PSA are located in the central region formed by leucine-rich repeats and that the IgG isotype produced during the natural infection is IgG2.

the identification of the immunodominants epitopes of the PSA protein and the determination of the immune humoral responses against them.
the identification of the immunogenic regions of the PSA and the determination of the isotype and subclass of the antibodies produced during the course of the disease.
the identification of the immunodominants in a protein from the surface of the parasite, which are the targets for the immune response in the natural host and the human patients.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the leucine rich repeat region is a major antigenic determinant in the PSA and that the IgG1 and especially the IgG2 are the main immunoglobulins produced during canine and human natural infections.
the leucine rich repeat region of the PSA is a major immunodominant epitope during the natural infection of dogs and humans by L. infantun.
the leucine rich repeat region of the PSA is the main immunodominant antigenic determinant of this protein during canine and human VL.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the immunodominance of the leucine rich regions of the PSA in dogs is a general feature of visceral leishmaniosis caused by L. (L.) infantum.
the central region of the PSA is a good antigen for the detection of canine and human visceral Leishmania infections.
the immunodominance of the leucine rich region of the PSA protein is a characteristic feature of the immune response in dogs and human visceral leshmaniasis caused L. infantum.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the leucine rich repeat region of PSA is the most immunodominant and that the IgG response is predominantly of the IgG2 isotype.
leucine rich repeat domains of the PSA are the main epitope of the parasite and that they can be used as a potential vaccine candidate.
the leucine rich region of the PSA is the main target for the immune system during natural infection.
